name: Yarra Valley

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Pinot Noir and Chardonnay sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

terms: Australia's Geographical Indications nest in three levels: zones, the regions inside them, and subregions inside those.
keyfacts: Traditional vineyards on the northern side of the valley have grey to grey-brown, low-fertility soils over red-brown clay subsoils.
Vineyards range from about ⟦elev|100 to 1,300 feet|30 to 400 m⟧, and the southern side, around Seville and Hoddles Creek, has much younger, deep, fertile red volcanic soils.
The Yarra Valley was Victoria's first wine-growing district, with vines planted in 1838 on the property now called Yering Station, but by 1937 all its vineyards had gone to pasture.

notes: Yarra Cabernet, often blended with a little Cabernet Franc and Merlot, ranges from medium to full bodied with silky tannins.
Yarra Chardonnay has moved away from the oaky, rich styles of the 1980s and 1990s toward fine, restrained wines, often picked at lower sugar levels to keep acidity high.

blurb.text: A cool-climate region east of Melbourne in the Port Phillip zone of Victoria, best known for Chardonnay, sparkling wine and Pinot Noir. Pinot Noir is 40% of plantings. It draws many visitors thanks to its closeness to the city.
